e-5589.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
e-5589.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$, where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/8b006c23e83405be4cd93396e5bde38c0dbcb5f8bb735b125d0b05f439e5b0d9.png)
e-5589.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/6fed2ac5452cf11059550a0c6328914c0e897714ca14a68f71df8eeb6d93471d.png)

We can find the least-squares solution ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by $A^T\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix $A^T \! A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $(A^T \! A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-5588.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
e-5588.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=12 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-12 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
e-5588.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/fa49e62c4e6fce14470e1641ef5e9a8c986778d74812e1bac82d3ba9df94aef8.png)

We can find the least-squares solution ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by $A^T\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix $A^T \! A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $(A^T \! A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,\,[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ -12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-24 \\ 0 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-24 \\ 0 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-7429.knowledge_point: Finding the Distance Between a Vector to a Subspace of Solutions of a Linear System
e-7429.problem:
Consider the system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $\Vert A\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b} \Vert.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/8200befaaea3a0cdec7e423999839c72d48fc67110fa577c8707e182c4524aff.png)
e-7429.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by $A^T\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix $A^T \! A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $(A^T \! A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}22 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}20 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}20 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}20 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $\Vert A\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{b} \Vert$ is attained when $\mathbf{x}={\hat{\mathbf{x}}},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$

In this case, $A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $\Vert A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \Vert$ is the distance between the vector $\mathbf{b}$ and the column space.

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\Vert A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}-\mathbf{b}\Vert =\sqrt{(-12)^2+0^2+(-12)^2+0^2}=12\sqrt{2}.
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
content.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the columns of A are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of Ax=b, where

A=[1021−1−110011−1] and b=[6060].

EXPLANATION

First of all, we write the given system in the form Ax=b:

[1021−1−110011−1]⏞A[x1x2x3]⏞x=[6060]⏞b

We can find the least-squares solution x^ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by AT:

ATAx^=ATb

Since the columns of A are linearly independent, the matrix ATA is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by (ATA)−1 on the left, we obtain

x^=(ATA)−1ATb=([11110−1012−10−1][1021−1−110011−1])−1[11110−1012−10−1][6060]=[400020006]−1[12012]=112[300060002][12012]=[302].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms A^T A = diag(4,2,6) and A^T b = (12,0,12)^T. Thus the normal equations give x̂ = (3,0,2)^T, option c. The observed incorrect submission selected option a.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
content.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 32 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 24\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{96}[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the columns of A are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of Ax=b, where

A=[2042−4−220024−2] and b=[120012].

EXPLANATION

First of all, we write the given system in the form Ax=b:

[2042−4−220024−2]⏞A[x1x2x3]⏞x=[120012]⏞b

We can find the least-squares solution x^ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by AT:

ATAx^=ATb

Since the columns of A are linearly independent, the matrix ATA is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by (ATA)−1 on the left, we obtain

x^=(ATA)−1ATb=([22220−4044−20−2][2042−4−220024−2])−1[22220−4044−20−2][120012]=[160003200024]−1[484824]=196[600030004][484824]=[3321].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
content.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 32 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 24\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{96}[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The normal equations give A^T A = diag(4,15) and A^T b = (8,-1)^T, since -2-6-2+9=-1. Thus the least-squares solution is (2,-1/15)^T, option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3 & 0\text{ }\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{60}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{60}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -\frac{1}{15}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{20} \\ -\frac{1}{20}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{20} \\ -\frac{1}{20}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 \\ 0 & 21\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -21\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{42}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 \\ -21\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 \\ 0 & 21\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -21\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{42}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 \\ -21\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

[940]

EXPLANATION

First of all, we write the given system in the form Ax=b: [1211−3012−11−10]⏞A[x1x2x3]⏞x=[180180]⏞b

We can find the least-squares solution x^ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by AT:

ATAx^=ATb

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=18 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=18 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 0 \\ 18 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 \\ 0 \\ 18 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}36 \\ 72 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}36 \\ 72 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=12 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=12\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=12 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=12\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=12\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & -16 \\ -16 & 29\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}29 & 16 \\ 16 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

[251925]

[31]

Correct
EXPLANATION

First of all, we write the given system in the form Ax=b: [2−3−1−23−4]⏞A[x1x2]⏞x=[−7−412]⏞b.

We can find the least-squares solution x^ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by AT:

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System
content.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=12\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & -16 \\ -16 & 29\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{150}[\begin{aligned}29 & 16 \\ 16 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}26 \\ -19\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 44\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}22 \\ 44\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -11 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{(-9)^{2}+(-11)^{2}+(-9)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=2\sqrt{71}.
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{30}.
$$

decision.explanation: The normal equations are 4x₁−5x₂=3 and −5x₁+7x₂=−9, giving x̂=(−8,−7)^T. The minimizing residual is (0,−1,−8,−7)^T, whose norm is √(1+64+49)=√114. Thus option e is correct.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 9 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ -5 & 7\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 9 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-7)^{2}}=\sqrt{114}.
$$

First of all, we write the given system in the form Ax=b:

[1−21−1−111−1]⏞A[x1x2]⏞x=[6096]⏞bAx=b

We can find the least-squares solution x^ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by AT:

ATAx^=ATb

Since the columns of A are linearly independent, the matrix ATA is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by (ATA)−1 on the left, we obtain

x^=(ATA)−1ATb=([11−11−2−11−1][1−21−1−111−1])−1[11−11−2−11−1][6096]=[4−5−57]−1[3−9]=13[7554][3−9]=[−8−7].

The minimum value of ‖Ax−b‖ is attained when x=x^, which is the least-squares solution of the system Ax=b. In this case, Ax^ represents the orthogonal projection of b onto the column space of A, and ‖Ax^−b‖ is the distance between the vector b and the column space. Therefore,

Ax^−b=[1−21−1−111−1][−8−7]−[6096]=[0−1−8−7].

Finally, ‖Ax^−b‖=02+(−1)2+(−8)2+(−7)2=114.

Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are shown below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]

after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ -8 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

content.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{3}.
$$
